title: Score a language model honestly
brief: Write bits per byte, a multiple-choice scorer, the unbiased pass@k estimator, bootstrap and paired bootstrap intervals, and an n-gram contamination check.
hints: Bits per byte is total_nats / (n_bytes * ln 2). A uniform model over 256 byte values has total_nats = n_bytes * ln 256, so it scores 8.0.
For options with totals [-6, -9, -12] and lengths [3, 6, 12], the raw argmax is option 0, and the per-byte scores [-2, -1.5, -1] give option 2.
pass_at_k(5, 2, 2): i runs over 4 and 5, so the product is (1 - 2/4) * (1 - 2/5) = 0.3 and the answer is 0.7. If n - c < k the factor i = k is exactly zero and the answer is 1.
Draw idx = rng.integers(0, n, size=(B, n)) once. scores[idx] has shape (B, n), and its mean over axis 1 is B resampled scores. Take np.percentile of those.
For the paired version, apply the same idx to both score arrays and take the difference of the two means on each resample.
Put every n-gram of every training document in one set of tuples. For test 'a b c d e', train 'x b c d y', n = 3, only ('b', 'c', 'd') is shared, so the overlap is 1/3.
